strategies.name: ict_stop_raid_mss_retracement_pd_array_entry
strategies.entry_summary: After establishing directional bias, wait for a stop raid/liquidity sweep, then a market structure shift/displacement in the intended direction. Enter on the retracement into discount/premium or OTE where a PD array is present, typically using a fair value gap, order block, breaker block, or a boxed
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop beyond the invalidation level of the entry structure (e.g. below the swing low for longs, above the order block/high for shorts). Take partials at opposing liquidity or prior highs/lows, optionally move stop to breakeven, and/or hold runners toward the next liquidity objective/new low

variants.variant_label: Long after sell-side raid into daily FVG, enter nested FVG/order block in OTE/bo
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for sell-side raid and structure shift up, then buy retracement into OTE with FVG nested in order block / box area
variants.target_note: first partial at buy-side liquidity; optional breakeven, then continuation higher

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches one core checklist-based retracement strategy with compatible PD-array variants (FVG, order block, breaker block, OTE, box setup) and one box/deviation example that lacks a separately runnable exit framework beyond the same shared management, so it is best treated as a variant/unpromoted mention rather than a distinct second strategy.
